### Learning Objectives {-}

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

- Apply fundamental dimensioning rules according to ASME Y14.5 standards
- Select appropriate dimension placement for clarity and manufacturability
- Use proper extension lines, dimension lines, and leaders
- Dimension common features including holes, arcs, and angles
- Avoid common dimensioning errors

::: {.callout-think}
**Before You Read:** Look at any mechanical part near you. How would you
communicate its exact size to someone who needs to manufacture it? What
measurements would be most important?
:::

### Introduction to Dimensioning

Dimensioning is the process of adding size and location information to
engineering drawings. Proper dimensioning ensures that parts can be
manufactured exactly as the designer intended.

::: {.callout-industry}
**Industry Connection:** In the defense industry, improper dimensioning can
have serious consequences. A famous example is the Mars Climate Orbiter, which
was lost due to a unit conversion error. Clear dimensioning standards prevent
such costly mistakes.
:::

### Try it yourself {#sec-tryit-dimensioning}

```{r tryit-dim-sort, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
tryit_sort(
  id = "dimension-practice",
  title = "Good practice or a dimensioning error?",
  bins = c("Good practice", "Dimensioning error"),
  cards = data.frame(
    text = c(
      "Each dimension is stated once on the drawing",
      "The same hole diameter is dimensioned in both the front view and the top view",
      "A dimension is placed on the view that shows the feature's shape most clearly",
      "A dimension is given to a hidden line instead of to a visible edge",
      "Dimensions are chosen to relate to the function of the part",
      "Numbers are given without units in a drawing that mixes inch and metric values and has no note",
      "Standard symbols and conventions are used so that anyone can read the drawing",
      "Several dimensions cross one another in a crowded view where space was available elsewhere"
    ),
    bin = c("Good practice", "Dimensioning error", "Good practice", "Dimensioning error",
            "Good practice", "Dimensioning error", "Good practice", "Dimensioning error"),
    why = c(
      "Repeating a dimension invites contradictions when the drawing is revised.",
      "A dimension should appear only once.",
      "Placement should be for maximum clarity.",
      "Do not dimension to hidden lines; use a visible edge or a section.",
      "Dimensions should relate to functional requirements.",
      "Unit confusion is how the Mars Climate Orbiter was lost.",
      "Standard symbols give universal understanding.",
      "Dimensions should be placed for clarity; crossing lines hide meaning."
    )
  ),
  intro = "Decide whether each practice follows the chapter's dimensioning rules.",
  question = "<p>Classify each practice as good dimensioning practice or a dimensioning error, using the rules of this chapter.</p>"
)
```

### Key Takeaways {-}

- Dimensions should be placed for maximum clarity
- Each dimension should appear only once on a drawing
- Dimensions should relate to functional requirements
- Standard symbols and conventions ensure universal understanding

::: {.callout-check}
**Quick Check:** What is the difference between an extension line and a
dimension line? Why is it important not to dimension to hidden lines?
:::
